source.title: I Am Large, I Contain Multitudes: Persona Transmission via Contextual Inference in LLMs

record.file_problem: Only a short post excerpt is provided; methods and detailed results are not included.
record.tranche_reason: Reports a prompt-context experiment about persona inference using a different signal and setup from fine-tuning on teacher-generated data.
record.gate_note: The excerpt reports a qualitative result for contextual inference from nonsensical questions paired with binary answers. It gives no numerical outcomes or named models. References to prior work are not treated as results from this post.
record.test_reason: The excerpt reports an in-context result: binary Yes/No answers to nonsensical questions encode a persona, and models act on it in safety questions. This is not fine-tuning on teacher outputs (A–C, E). It does not insert the linked or entangled tokens that F names; the post designs its contrast to exclude entangled tokens. It tests no subliminal-learning mechanism (D). It also offers no numbers or named models. It is a related construct (contextual self-consistency inference), so it goes under fits_no_version rather than as a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim that LLMs infer past personas from binary answers to nonsensical questions in context and act on them in safety-related questions. They frame the effect as contextual-inference self-consistency, isolated from the entangled-token effect behind subliminal learning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an in-context sequence of nonsensical questions and binary answers rather than fine-tuning on filtered teacher-generated outputs.
record.method_sensitivity: The contrasting encoding contexts differ in their binary answers while most question content is held identical.

fits_no_version.finding: Models reportedly infer a past persona from Yes/No answers to nonsensical questions held in context, and act on it in safety-related questions. The contrasting contexts differ only in the answers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-only persona transmission via contextual self-consistency inference from semantically unrelated, low-bit context, distinct from token entanglement.

record.problems: The supplied excerpt does not identify models, give experimental details, provide numerical results or uncertainty, or specify the safety-related behaviors measured.
record.rows_left_out: No other study results are reported in the supplied excerpt.

rows.subject: LLMs
rows.operation_detail: Presented an in-context encoding of past personas using nonsensical questions paired with Yes/No answers, then tested safety-related questions.

conditions.value: the versions differed in the binary answers; most question content was identical

rows.measure: Qualitative report of inferring information about past personas and acting on it in safety-related questions
rows.baseline: Contrasting encoding context with different binary answers; specific outcome not stated
rows.value: The post says models infer persona information and act upon it; no rate or specific behaviors stated
rows.note: The authors characterize the questions as semantically unrelated to the target misalignment behaviors and the answers as providing one bit each. This is a related prompt-only analogue, not a reported test using the linked tokens from the original study.
rows.check: Linked to D and F wrongly. F concerns inserting the tokens linked by subliminal learning; this encodes personas through binary answers, which the authors set apart from token entanglement. D concerns what carries the signal in subliminal learning; no candidate mechanism is tested. The subject is unnamed ('LLMs'), the baseline outcome is not stated and no value is given. 'Observed' reflects only the authors' qualitative claim.
